_comment: Night Shift permission settings. tools/night_shift.sh installs this file as
.claude/settings.local.json is gitignored, so the tracked copy is this one).
and --permission-prompts none. The allow list below approves every tool, so nothing
ever waits on a prompt; the deny list wins over every allow (user-level allows for
`pio run -e teensy41 -t upload` included), which the P1 probe confirmed: a denied
Bash call is refused and itemised under permission_denials in the JSON result.
The bridge is powered at night and its UDP link is single-owner; the robot is not
powered. Nothing here may reach either: no flash, no launch, no hardware script, no
system service, and never a write under the live checkout ~/Desktop/Jugglebot.
A pattern with a leading * matches anywhere in the command line, so `cd X && pio run`
is caught too. Edit this file, never the installed copy.

The Bash deny list is best-effort pattern matching, not a sandbox: it stops the obvious spellings of every forbidden action so an honest orchestrator cannot stumble into one; the hold file, the live-Sitting guard and the merge gate are the layers that do not depend on spelling.

A deny rule beats every allow, so a rule that matches a word also blocks reading and testing that word. Until 2026-11-07 *teensy_bridge_node* and *teensy_link* refused greps and the bridge's own loopback tests while the night's gate ran those same tests anyway. These rules now name the spellings that RUN the node or the client; the protection for a test is tools/night_shift_nonet.sh, a network namespace where the board is unreachable whatever the command does.

Probes and bag reads (closeout C7a, 2026-11-14) are allowed ONLY under tools/night_shift_nonet.sh, which binds ~/Desktop/rosbags and ~/.ros/log read-only, masks the serial devices and has no network. No pattern can demand that prefix, so the rules below anchor on the UNWRAPPED spellings instead (no leading *: a line that starts with python, timeout, cd tools/probes, ros2 bag, ... or has one after &&, ; or |), which the wrapped form never matches because it starts with the wrapper. The wrapper goes first and timeout/env go after it. ros2 bag play, record, reindex and convert stay refused even wrapped.
pio test is denied because bare pio test builds for the ESP32 and tries to upload; the native run is tests/firmware/test_wave_native.py, which can only pass -e native.
